Q: Round a divided number in Bash A:

If the decimal separator is comma (e.g., LC_NUMERIC=fr_FR.UTF-8, see here):

printf "%.0f" $(echo "scale=2;3/2" | bc)

Output:

bash: printf: 1.50: nombre non valable
0

Substitution is needed for ghostdog74's solution:

printf "%.0f" $(echo "scale=2;3/2" | bc | sed 's/[.]/,/')

Output:

2

Or

printf "%.0f" $(echo "scale=2;3/2" | bc | tr '.' ',')

Output:

2

Q: Hibernate showing non unique object exception during bulk insert of parent entity with Cascade All. Tried all possibilities A:

Hibernate is saying that you have two objects which have the same primary identifier but they are not the same object.

It most often happens via cascading saves where there is a cascade save between ParentEntity and ChildEntity, but ChildEntity has already been associated with the session but not on the same instance of ChildEntity.

Q: How to create smooth interpolations between two images with OpenCV? A:

I won't go too much into rotating the homograph. I do not understand why you want to do that or what you expect. If you want to see the image to be warped slowly distorting (translate, scale an rotate), get the four corners of each image. Then slowly rotate, scale and translate those coordinates of the image to be warped until they align with your reference image. Then for each adjustment create an affine or perspective transform (homography) and then do an affine warp until the two images align.

Skipping that, here is one way to warp the one image onto the other using ORB and perspective warp in Python OpenCV.

(An affine warp may be sufficient. But I did not know if there was any slight perspective distortions to either image)

  • Read the two images

  • Convert them to grayscale

  • Use ORB to get keypoints and descriptors

  • Match the features using with a Brute Force Matcher and Hamming distance

  • Sort the match by distance so best match is first

  • Keep only the top 50 matches

  • Make sure there are enough good matches

  • Find the homography

  • Warp img2 to match img2

  • Save the warped image

  • Define a delay and show alternating images until a key is pressed on the keyboard

Reference image (img1):

Image to be warped (img2):

import cv2
import numpy as np

# Load the images
img1 = cv2.imread('top_view1.jpg')  # Reference i.e., Destination image
img2 = cv2.imread('top_view2.jpg')  # Image to be warped to match reference image

# Convert the images to graysccale
gray1 = cv2.cvtColor(img1, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
gray2 = cv2.cvtColor(img2, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)

# Detect keypoints and descriptors using ORB
orb = cv2.ORB_create(nfeatures=1000)
keypoints1, descriptors1 = orb.detectAndCompute(gray1, None)
keypoints2, descriptors2 = orb.detectAndCompute(gray2, None)

# Match features using Brute-Force Matcher with Hamming distance
bf = cv2.BFMatcher(cv2.NORM_HAMMING, crossCheck=True)
matches = bf.match(descriptors1, descriptors2)

# Sort matches by distance (best matches first)
matches = sorted(matches, key=lambda x: x.distance)

# Keep only the top matches
good_matches = matches[:50]

# Make sure there are enough matches to calculate homography
if len(good_matches) > 10:
    # Extract location of matching points
    # Note: queryIdx is img1 (destination), trainIdx is img2 (source)
    dst_pts = np.float32([keypoints1[m.queryIdx].pt for m in good_matches]).reshape(-1, 1, 2)
    src_pts = np.float32([keypoints2[m.trainIdx].pt for m in good_matches]).reshape(-1, 1, 2)

    # Find the homography matrix using RANSAC
    H, mask = cv2.findHomography(src_pts, dst_pts, cv2.RANSAC, 5.0)

    # Warp img2 to match img1 via perspective
    height, width, channels = img1.shape
    img2_warped = cv2.warpPerspective(img2, H, (width, height))

    # Save result
    cv2.imwrite('warped_image2_orb.jpg', img2_warped)
    
    # show results
    # Define delay in milliseconds (e.g., 500ms = 0.5 seconds per image)
    delay_ms = 500

    print("Displaying alternating images. Press any key on your keyboard to exit")

    # Keep track of which image to show
    show_flag = True

    while True:
        # Select which image to display
        current_image = img1 if show_flag else img2_warped
        window_name = "Image Comparison"
        cv2.imshow(window_name, current_image)
    
        # Wait until a key is pressed (then it returns a key code (> -1))
        key = cv2.waitKey(delay_ms)
    
        if key != -1:
            # A key was pressed, so break the loop
            break
        
        # Toggle the boolean flag for the next iteration
        show_flag = not show_flag

    cv2.destroyAllWindows()

else:
    print("Not enough good matching points found")

Q: What compiler options can detect signed integer overflow? A:

You can use -fsanitize=undefined with gcc. Then gcc produces:

/app/example.cpp:7:60: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 4096 * 1048576 cannot be represented in type 'int'

Unfortunately, msvc doesn't have an equivalent flag that can directly detect this. But msvc does provide you with static analysis mode using /analyze option that will let you detect this as shown in this answer. So, you do have an option to detect this with msvc as well.

Q: Controller hotplugging issue A:

I think you need to initialise the controllers and track them using a dictionary or a list.

Without joystick.init() the controllers are not being activated and ready to use. This is separate from the pygame.init(), it has it's own life cycle.

Try this example:

import pygame

pygame.joystick.init()
joysticks = [pygame.joystick.Joystick(x) for x in range(pygame.joystick.get_count())]

print(joysticks)

So in your case you want to listen to the adding event:

joysticks = {}
if event.type == pygame.JOYDEVICEADDED:
    joystick = pygame.joystick.Joystick(event.device_index) 
    joystick.init()

    joysticks[joystick.get_instance_id()] = joystick

    print("Added:", joystick.get_name())

Make sure you remove the controller from the list when it's disconnected:

elif event.type == pygame.JOYDEVICEREMOVED:
    joysticks.pop(event.instance_id, None)
    print("Removed:", event.instance_id)

However in your case i see the device index are both 0 so am not sure what will happen, but you can use get_count as in the example above and track them yourself, or maybe use the guid. Its up to you, use what works in your case.
